prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study describes a 54-year-old woman who experienced head and neck pain for eight days and worsening weakness in her left arm for four days.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A neurological exam indicated that the left C5-C6 nerve roots or the upper part of the brachial plexus were affected.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Standard scans of the neck and shoulder showed age-related and muscle-bone issues, but these did not fully account for the quick loss of strength in the upper arm.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: An MRI of the brachial plexus showed that the left C5 nerve root was larger and had a brighter signal than the nerve on the other side.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A focused ultrasound scan found a localized widening of the left vertebral artery with signs of a tear and pressure on nearby nerves.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A specialized X-ray test using contrast dye confirmed the presence of a dissecting aneurysm in the left vertebral artery.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The patient received a procedure to place a stent inside the artery to repair it.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: After the procedure, her neck and shoulder pain significantly decreased and the strength in her left arm slowly returned.
facts.subject: humans
